class_data.name: Spellcasting
class_data.notes:
You have learned to cast spells as a student of arcane magic.

Cantrips. You know three Wizard cantrips of your choice (Light, Mage Hand, and Ray of Frost are recommended). Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace one of these cantrips with another Wizard cantrip of your choice. At Wizard levels 4 and 10, you learn one additional Wizard cantrip, as shown in the class table.

Spellbook. Your studies culminated in the creation of your spellbook. It is a Tiny object (3 pounds, 100 pages) that can be read only by you or by someone casting Identify. You determine its appearance and materials.
The book contains the level 1+ Wizard spells you know. It begins with six level 1 Wizard spells of your choice (Detect Magic, Feather Fall, Mage Armor, Magic Missile, Sleep, and Thunderwave are recommended).
Whenever you gain a Wizard level after 1, you add two Wizard spells of your choice to your spellbook. Each spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots, as shown in the Wizard Features table.

Spell Slots. The Wizard Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a Long Rest.

Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare a list of Wizard spells of level 1+ that you can cast. To start, choose four spells from your spellbook. Each prepared spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.
The number of prepared spells increases as you gain Wizard levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Wizard Features table; whenever that number increases, you choose additional spells from your spellbook to match the new total.
If another Wizard feature gives you spells that are always prepared, those spells don’t count against the number of spells you can prepare, but they count as Wizard spells for you.

Changing Prepared Spells. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change your list of prepared spells, replacing any of them with other spells from your spellbook.

Spellcasting Ability. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for Wizard spells.

Spellcasting Focus. You can use an Arcane Focus or your spellbook as a Spellcasting Focus for your Wizard spells.

Expanding and Replacing a Spellbook. The spells you gain when leveling reflect your ongoing research, but you can also add spells you find:
• Copying a Spell into the Book. When you find a level 1+ Wizard spell, you can copy it into your spellbook if it is of a level you can prepare and you have the time and resources. Copying takes 2 hours and 50 GP per spell level. Once copied, you can prepare the spell like any other in your book.
• Copying the Book. You can copy spells from your spellbook into another book. This is faster because you already know the spells: it takes 1 hour and 10 GP per spell level.
• Replacing a Lost Book. If you lose your spellbook, you can use the same process to transcribe the Wizard spells you currently have prepared into a new book. Filling out the remainder of the new spellbook requires you to find additional spells. Many wizards keep a backup spellbook for this reason.

class_data.name: Ritual Adept
class_data.notes: You can cast any spell as a Ritual if the spell has the Ritual tag and is in your spellbook. You need not have the spell prepared, but you must read from your spellbook when casting it as a Ritual.

class_data.name: Arcane Recovery
class_data.notes:
You can regain some of your magical energy by studying your spellbook. When you finish a Short Rest, you can recover expended spell slots with a combined level equal to no more than half your Wizard level (round up), and none of the recovered slots can be level 6 or higher.
For example, as a level 4 Wizard, you can recover up to two levels’ worth of spell slots (one level 2 slot or two level 1 slots).
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

class_data.name: Scholar
class_data.notes: In addition to your magical studies, you specialized in another field of study. Choose one of the following skills in which you have proficiency: Arcana, History, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, or Religion. You gain Expertise in the chosen skill.

class_data.name: Subclass Feature
class_data.notes:
You choose a Wizard subclass and gain its level 3 feature. You gain additional subclass features at higher Wizard levels.

class_data.name: Ability Score Improvement
class_data.notes: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Wizard levels 8, 12, and 16.

class_data.name: Memorize Spell
class_data.notes: Whenever you finish a Short Rest, you can study your spellbook and replace one of the level 1+ Wizard spells you have prepared for your Spellcasting feature with a different level 1+ Wizard spell from your spellbook.

class_data.name: Spell Mastery
class_data.notes:
You achieve mastery over certain spells and can cast them at will. Choose a level 1 Wizard spell and a level 2 Wizard spell from your spellbook that each have a casting time of an action.
You always have these spells prepared, and you can cast them at their lowest level without expending a spell slot. To cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend an appropriate spell slot.
Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can study your spellbook and replace one or both of these spells with other eligible spells of the same levels from your spellbook.

class_data.name: Epic Boon
class_data.notes: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Spell Recall is recommended.

class_data.name: Signature Spells
class_data.notes:
You choose two level 3 Wizard spells from your spellbook as your signature spells.
You always have these spells prepared, and you can cast each of them once at level 3 without expending a spell slot. When you cast a signature spell in this way, you can’t do so again with that spell until you finish a Short or Long Rest.
To cast a signature spell at a higher level, you must expend an appropriate spell slot.

subclass_data.name: Evocation Savant
subclass_data.notes:
Add two free level 1–2 Evocation Wizard spells to your spellbook.
Whenever you gain a new level of spell slots, add one free Evocation spell of a level you can cast.

subclass_data.name: Potent Cantrip
subclass_data.notes: When you cast a damaging cantrip and miss the attack or the target succeeds on its save, the target still takes half damage (no additional effects apply on the failed/full save).

subclass_data.name: Sculpt Spells
subclass_data.notes: When casting an Evocation spell that affects other visible creatures, choose a number of creatures equal to 1 + the spell’s level. They automatically succeed on the saving throw and take no damage on a successful-save-for-half spell.

subclass_data.name: Empowered Evocation
subclass_data.notes: Add your Intelligence modifier to one damage roll of any Evocation Wizard spell you cast.

subclass_data.name: Overchannel
subclass_data.notes:
When you cast a level 1–5 Wizard spell that deals damage, you may maximize its damage dice.
• First use per Long Rest: no drawback.
• Subsequent uses before finishing a Long Rest: take 2d12 Necrotic damage per spell level. This damage ignores Resistance and Immunity.
• Each additional use increases the damage by +1d12 per spell level (e.g., second use 2d12/level, third 3d12/level, etc.).

effects.name: Resourceful
effects.notes: You gain Heroic Inspiration whenever you finish a Long Rest.

effects.name: Skillful
effects.notes: You gain proficiency in one skill of your choice.

effects.name: Versatile
effects.notes: You gain an Origin feat of your choice.

feats.notes: Two Cantrips. You learn two cantrips of your choice from the Cleric, Druid, or Wizard spell list. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this feat's spells (choose when you select this feat).Level 1 Spell. Choose a level 1 spell from the same list you selected for this feat's cantrips. You always have that spell prepared. You can cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have.Spell Change. Whenever you gain a new level, you can replace one of the spells you chose for this feat with a different spell of the same level from the chosen spell list.
feats.name: Magic Initiate (Druid)

feats.notes: Mounted Strike. While mounted, you have Advantage on attack rolls against any unmounted creature within 5 feet of your mount that is at least one size smaller than the mount.Leap Aside. If your mount is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, it instead takes no damage if it succeeds on the saving throw and only half damage if it fails. For your mount to gain this benefit, you must be riding it, and neither of you can have the Incapacitated condition.Veer. While mounted, you can force an attack that hits your mount to hit you instead if you don't have the Incapacitated condition.
feats.name: Mounted Combatant

feats.notes: mproved Dash. When you take the Dash action, your Speed increases by 10 feet for that action.Charge Attack. If you move at least 10 feet in a straight line toward a target immediately before hitting it with a melee attack roll as part of the Attack action, choose one of the following effects: gain a 1d8 bonus to the attack's damage roll, or push the target up to 10 feet away if it is no more than one size larger than you. You can use this benefit only once on each of your turns.
feats.name: Charger

feats.notes: Cook's Utensils. You gain proficiency with Cook's Utensils if you don't already have it.Replenishing Meal. As part of a Short Rest, you can cook special food if you have ingredients and Cook's Utensils on hand. You can prepare enough of this food for a number of creatures equal to 4 plus your Proficiency Bonus. At the end of the Short Rest, any creature who eats the food and spends one or more Hit Dice to regain Hit Points regains an extra 1d8 Hit Points.Bolstering Treats. With 1 hour of work or when you finish a Long Rest, you can cook a number of treats equal to your Proficiency Bonus if you have ingredients and Cook's Utensils on hand. These special treats last 8 hours after being made. A creature can use a Bonus Action to eat one of those treats to gain a number of Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
feats.name: Chef

feats.notes: Escape Artist. As a Bonus Action, you can take the Disengage action, which also ends the Grappled condition on you.Quickness. Your Speed increases by 30 feet.
feats.name: Boon of Speed
